title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to test whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on intent→configuration NetOps tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes) with model_calls_used = 200 and repair calls invoked = 0. Both baseline and guarded conditions passed the deterministic oracle for all 200 pairs (baseline = 200/200; guarded = 200/200). The paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. The null result is design‑bound: shared_initial_candidate semantics produced identical passing candidates for both arms, so repairs were never exercised. We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for follow‑ups that permit repair invocation (independent generation, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being evaluated as intent→configuration agents for network operations (NetOps). A common mitigation pattern for LLM misconfiguration risk is generate→validate→repair: produce a candidate configuration, deterministically validate objective properties (reachability, protected resources, transient safety), and, on failure, invoke a repair generator guided by validator evidence. Prior work shows constraint‑guided generation or verifier‑grounded repair can reduce misconfiguration in some settings, but rigorous, preregistered, fully archived comparisons that exercise the repair stage are rare. We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to provide a confirmatory, artifact‑auditable measurement of verifier benefit under a frozen experimental plan. The preregistration fixed generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), repair budget (≤1 call/task), and the paired analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). All artifacts from the autonomous run (prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, manifests, and per‑file SHA‑256 digests) are archived for reproducibility (see provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The principal contribution reported here is an evidence‑anchored account of the preregistered run, deterministic artifact reconciliation, precise statistical reporting, and concrete artifact‑grounded recommendations for informative follow‑ups.
sections.related_work: Work relevant to intent→configuration and verifier‑assisted pipelines includes constraint‑guided LLM adaptation and verifier‑grounded repair workflows. Representative references drawn from the provided evidence bundle include MeshAgent (constraint‑based adaptation for NetOps), NetConfEval (intent→configuration benchmarks in NetOps), and verifier‑grounded program repair exemplars (StruSpec). These works motivated our preregistration choices (validator semantics, formal oracle checks) and guided our emulation‑based oracle design. Unlike many prior publications, our run was preregistered, executed autonomously, and archived with per‑artifact SHA‑256 digests enabling deterministic reconciliation and auditor verification.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design: The experiment was preregistered as study‑cnd‑2026‑001 (SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2). Key frozen choices included the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generator call per pair shared by both arms), declared model gpt‑5‑mini via adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1, deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, task stratification, and the paired analysis (paired bootstrap + McNemar). The preregistration specified complete‑pair primary analysis and registered sensitivity analyses.

Task bank and stratification: The confirmatory sample comprised 200 pairs stratified by protocol and vendor: 4 protocol buckets (BGP, OSPF, ACL, VLAN) with 50 pairs each; per protocol vendor allocation Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (total Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64). Complexity split: 100 simple, 100 complex. Each task manifest entry (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) contains explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, intent text, required_sequence, and constraint metadata (allowed_touched_fields, workflow policies). Representative manifests and reference answers are archived (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c30860...).

Generation, validator, and repair mechanics: The generator call semantics used shared_initial_candidate: exactly one generator invocation per pair produced a single candidate artifact that the baseline and guarded scoring/validation consumed. The deterministic validator parsed the candidate, simulated the canonical emulated network model, produced normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, final_state, valid boolean, and a validator trace that records which semantic predicates were exercised and whether repair was applied. The repair module was permitted by preregistration but not invoked in practice (repair_applied = false in all validator traces). All provider calls, raw responses, and scoring outputs were immutably archived and SHA‑256 hashed (execution/execution_manifest.json lists >1,300 artifacts and per‑file digests).

Analysis plan: The primary confirmatory analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1: paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) to estimate a 95% percentile CI for the paired success‑rate difference, plus an exact two‑sided McNemar test for discordant pairs. Missingness policy: complete‑pair primary analysis (pairs where either condition fails due to provider/infrastructure failure are excluded); the run produced no such failures and zero exclusions. All analysis artifacts are archived under analysis/ with digests.
sections.results:
Execution and raw outcomes (artifact backed): The autonomous run completed as preregistered: planned episodes = 400; completed episodes = 400; failed episodes = 0; model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generator call per pair). Scoring summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4...): baseline_successes = 200/200 (100%); guarded_successes = 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...) is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0.

Confirmatory inference (artifact: analysis/results.json): paired estimate = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. The analysis log and bootstrap settings are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 940b48e7...). Representative per‑task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/task-000001‑baseline.json etc.) record normalized configurations, parsed_command_count, validator final_state maps, and repair_applied=false. Repair_calls_invoked = 0 across the entire run; no repair prompts or repair provider traces were produced.

Deterministic reconciliation and accounting: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms complete_pair_count = 200, hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and that provider call and scoring records are consistently cross‑referenced with per‑file SHA‑256 digests (execution/execution_manifest.json). All deterministic consistency checks passed.

Representative examples (artifact pointers): task‑000001 shows a medium‑difficulty shutdown→configure→restore sequence where the shared candidate matched the reference answer and validator reported valid=true (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec...). Similar artifact pairs for tasks 000002–000006 and beyond are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and causal explanation of the null result: The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one generated candidate per pair that both conditions consumed. In this run every shared candidate satisfied the deterministic validator, so the repair stage never triggered (repair_calls_invoked = 0). Consequently, the guarded arm had no opportunity to improve over baseline; the observed null effect (paired difference = 0.00) is therefore a direct consequence of the preregistered generation semantics and the chosen task/model behavior rather than evidence that verifier assistance can never help. The result correctly answers the preregistered estimand under the frozen design and highlights the methodological necessity of allowing generator variance and oracle failures when the objective is to measure repair effectiveness.

Operational implications and artifact‑grounded recommendations: To measure repair benefit reliably, an experimental design must permit the repair module to act. We provide two artifact‑supported, low‑risk follow‑ups (all reproducible from the archived prompts and manifests): (1) change generation_semantics to independent_per_condition so each arm receives an independently sampled candidate (expected model_calls ≈ 400); this converts the within‑pair comparison into a valid test of guard+repair vs baseline under generator stochasticity; (2) increase task difficulty (append higher‑difficulty tasks to execution/task_manifest.jsonl or adversarialize boundary conditions) so some generator outputs fail the deterministic validator and trigger repair. Both variants are supported by the provided tooling and manifests and will be fully auditable (new runs will produce new per‑file SHA‑256 digests). Additional knobs: raise maximum_repair_calls_per_task > 1 to permit iterative repair loops, or run multi‑model replications to test generality.

Threats to validity (artifact‑anchored): Internal validity — the crucial internal validity consideration is generation semantics (frozen). Construct validity — our deterministic validator enforces objective emulation‑based checks (reachability, protected interfaces, required sequences), but oracle blind spots can exist; validator traces record which predicates were exercised and any ambiguous coverage flags. External validity — the run used one declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and emulated device models rather than live vendor hardware; results therefore do not generalize beyond those limits. Conclusion validity — the paired design and preregistered analysis were executed faithfully; inference is exact for the frozen estimand but degenerate due to no discordant pairs. All of these points are substantiated in the archived artifacts and reconciliation files.
sections.conclusion: Under the exact preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics, verifier assistance produced no measurable benefit because the shared generated candidate passed the deterministic oracle for every pair and repairs were never exercised. The run demonstrates the importance of aligning generation semantics, task difficulty, and repair budget with the scientific question: to test the efficacy of repairs the experiment must allow generator variability and oracle failures. We publish the full artifact bundle (preregistration, master prompt reference, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) to enable reproducible follow‑ups that remove the ceiling effect (independent generation semantics, higher difficulty tasks, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests).

This initial master prompt launched the autonomous post‑lock research run. The Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) pre‑lock; all substantive research actions reported here were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock.
- Preregistration (frozen): study id = study-cnd-2026-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2. The preregistration froze the research question, primary estimand, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, deterministic validator, repair budget, sampling plan, stopping rules, and analysis executor.
- LLM(s) and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini accessed via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Model configuration artifact execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa) records the declared model metadata used during the run. All provider calls and raw responses are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json (artifact bundle).
- Generation semantics and intervention: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (frozen). Under this semantics exactly one generator call was made per pair and the identical generated candidate was supplied to both baseline and guarded scoring/validation. This preregistered choice reduced generator calls (model_calls_used = 200) but produced a ceiling effect: every shared candidate passed the deterministic validator and repairs were never invoked.
- Validator, repair policy, and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed deterministic syntactic+semantic checks and emulation‑based validation of required sequences; representative scoring artifacts are archived (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860...). Maximum_repair_calls_per_task was preregistered as 1; in this run repair_applied = false for every pair and repair provider traces were not produced.
- Analysis procedures: primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4...) and the analysis log (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 940b48e7...) are archived.
- Execution and reproducibility: every prompt, model output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record, manifest, and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 digests. Deterministic reconciliation artifact analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 = 799b23b9...) verifies accounting consistency (complete_pair_count = 200; model_calls_used = 200; repair_calls_invoked = 0). The full execution manifest lists >1,300 artifacts with per‑file SHA‑256 values.
- Human involvement statement: Pre‑lock collaborative infrastructure development and topic selection were performed by the Research Director. After the autonomy lock, the AI system autonomously conducted literature search, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting and revision. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript body after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock artifacts were explicitly excluded from serving as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations and known limitations: the only substantive design choice that produced the observed ceiling effect is the preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation semantics; this is documented in the preregistration artifact and the execution manifest. All deviations from the preregistration (none affecting primary analysis) and all provider/infrastructure events are recorded in the execution manifest.
limitations: The confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated 200‑pair task bank).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the repair stage was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0), preventing any measurable guarded benefit in this run.

Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture production heterogeneity (real vendor images, device nondeterminism, runtime quirks); external validity is therefore limited.
Single declared model limits generality; multi‑model replications remain necessary to assess model dependence.
The repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies were not explored in this run.
Oracle blind spots remain possible; validator coverage diagnostics are archived per pair and should be inspected when extending the study.
